2008B16.goal: Two coins are tossed; each head earns one die roll. We want $P(\text{sum of dice is odd})$, with no dice meaning sum $0$. Split by the number of heads.

tools.name: Law of total probability
tools.why: The number of dice depends on the coins.

tools.name: Parity of dice sums
tools.why: One die is odd half the time; adding another fair die keeps it at $\tfrac12$.

2008B16.approach: $0$ heads ($\tfrac14$): sum $0$, even. $1$ head ($\tfrac12$): odd with $\tfrac12$. $2$ heads ($\tfrac14$): odd with $\tfrac12$.

check.q: What is $P(\text{exactly one head in two tosses})$?
What is $\tfrac14+\tfrac18$?

2008B16.bridge: Condition on the number of heads.
solution: One or two heads: odd with probability $\tfrac12$.
traps: Treating "no dice" as odd or ignoring it ($\tfrac12$).
2008B16.recognize: Random number of random trials: condition on how many trials happen.

2008B17.goal: Each of $3$ independent random voters approves with probability $0.7$. We want $P(\text{exactly one approves})$. This is a binomial probability.

tools.name: Binomial formula
tools.why: Choose which trials succeed; multiply independent probabilities.

check.q: What is $0.7\cdot0.09$?

steps.title: All patterns
steps.explain: The approver can be any of $3$ occasions: $3\cdot0.063=0.189$.

check.q: How many ways can exactly one of three be the approver?

2008B17.bridge: Multiply one pattern's probability by the number of patterns.
2008B17.shortcut: Answer (A) is the trap of a single order.
2008B17.recognize: "Exactly $k$ of $n$ independent trials": binomial coefficient times the pattern probability.

2008B18.goal: Brenda alone takes $9$ h, Brandon $10$ h; together their rate drops by $10$ bricks/h, and they finish in $5$ h. We want the number of bricks $N$.

tools.name: Combined rate
tools.why: Combined output equals the job over $5$ hours.

check.q: What is $\tfrac19+\tfrac1{10}$?
If $\tfrac{N}{90}=10$, what is $N$?

2008B18.bridge: Set the reduced combined rate equal to $N/5$.
2008B18.shortcut: Test choices: $900$ gives rates $100$ and $90$, combined $180$, and $180\cdot5=900$. ✓
traps: Subtracting $10$ bricks total instead of per hour.
2008B18.recognize: Work problems: add rates, not times.

2008B19.goal: A cylinder (radius $4$, length $9$) lies on its side with water $2$ ft deep. Volume = (area of the circular segment) × $9$. The water surface is a chord $2$ below the centre.

tools.name: Segment area
tools.why: The water cross-section is the region below a chord.

tools.name: Central angle
tools.why: The chord is $2$ from the centre; half-angle $60^\circ$, full $120^\circ$.

2008B19.approach: Central angle $120^\circ$. Sector: $\tfrac13\cdot16\pi$. Triangle: $\tfrac12\cdot4\cdot4\sin120^\circ=4\sqrt3$. Segment $\tfrac{16\pi}3-4\sqrt3$; multiply by $9$.

steps.title: Angle
steps.explain: Distance from centre to chord $=4-2=2$; $\cos\tfrac\theta2=\tfrac24$, so $\theta=120^\circ$.

check.q: If the half-angle has cosine $\tfrac12$, what is the full central angle?
What is $\tfrac12\cdot4\cdot4\cdot\sin120^\circ$?

2008B19.bridge: Segment area (sector minus triangle) times length.
2008B19.shortcut: Sanity check: $48\pi-36\sqrt3\approx88.4$, about $20\%$ of the full $144\pi$.
traps: Adding the triangle instead of subtracting.
2008B19.recognize: Liquid in a horizontal cylinder: circular segment area times length.

2008B20.goal: Die 1: $1,2,2,3,3,4$. Die 2: $1,3,4,5,6,8$. We want $P(\text{sum}\in\{5,7,9\})$. Count over the $36$ face pairs.
2008B20.approach: For each value $v$ on die 1, count die-2 faces in $\{5-v,7-v,9-v\}$.

check.q: For $v=2$, which faces of die 2 work?
Simplify $\tfrac{14}{36}$.

2008B20.bridge: Count favourable face pairs, dividing by $36$.
2008B20.shortcut: Only odd sums qualify; the only odd sums that fail are $3$ and $11$, rarer to count.
traps: Counting the repeated $2$ and $3$ only once.
2008B20.recognize: Non-standard dice: count face pairs directly.

2008B21.goal: Five couples sit at $10$ numbered chairs, alternating men and women, with nobody next to or across from their spouse. Seat the men first, then count the ways to seat the women.

tools.name: Across is opposite parity
tools.why: $5$ is odd, so the across seat is a woman's seat.

tools.name: Allowed-seat graph
tools.why: Two neighbours and the across seat are banned.

2008B21.approach: Men take odd or even chairs ($2$) in $5!$ orders. Each wife then has exactly $2$ allowed chairs; those choices link up into one $10$-cycle, which has exactly $2$ perfect matchings.

check.q: What is $2\cdot5!$?

steps.title: Women
steps.explain: With men in chairs $1,3,5,7,9$: wife of chair $1$ may use $4,8$; of $3$: $6,10$; of $5$: $2,8$; of $7$: $4,10$; of $9$: $2,6$. These form one cycle, so there are $2$ ways. Total $240\cdot2=480$.

check.q: How many perfect matchings does a single cycle of length $10$ (alternating wives and chairs) have?
check.why: Pick alternate edges in one of two ways.

2008B21.bridge: Seat men, then match wives to allowed chairs.
solution: Each wife has $2$ allowed chairs; the constraints form one cycle with $2$ matchings.
2008B21.shortcut: Once the first wife chooses between her $2$ chairs, everything else is forced.
traps: Forgetting the factor $2$ for which parity the men use.
Forgetting that across seats are women's seats.
2008B21.recognize: Restricted seatings: fix one group, then each restriction becomes an allowed-seat graph.

2008B22.goal: Beads $RRRWWB$ in a random line. We want $P(\text{no two neighbours match})$. Place the three reds first: no two adjacent.
2008B22.approach: Red positions: $\{1,3,5\},\{2,4,6\},\{1,3,6\},\{1,4,6\}$. Fill the other three spots with $W,W,B$ keeping the whites apart.

steps.title: Red placements
steps.explain: $\{1,3,5\}$ and $\{2,4,6\}$ leave three separated spots: $3$ ways each (where $B$ goes). $\{1,3,6\}$ leaves $2,4,5$ and $\{1,4,6\}$ leaves $2,3,5$: one adjacent pair, so $B$ must go in it: $2$ ways each.

check.q: Reds at $1,3,6$: spots $2,4,5$ remain. In how many ways can $W,W,B$ go without adjacent whites?
What is $\tfrac{10}{60}$?

2008B22.bridge: Place the most common colour first, then fill.
2008B22.shortcut: Place the most frequent colour first — it is the hardest to separate.
traps: Using $6!$ with identical beads unadjusted inconsistently.
2008B22.recognize: "No two adjacent alike": place the most common item first in non-adjacent spots.

2008B23.goal: An $a\times b$ floor ($b>a$, integers) has a painted rectangle with a $1$-ft border, and the border is half the floor. Count the pairs $(a,b)$. The painted part is $(a-2)(b-2)=\tfrac{ab}2$.

tools.name: Simon's factoring trick
tools.why: Add $16-8$ to both sides to factor.

tools.name: Factor pairs
tools.why: Positive pairs with the smaller first.

2008B23.approach: $2(a-2)(b-2)=ab$ expands to $ab-4a-4b+8=0$, i.e. $(a-4)(b-4)=8$. Check positive and negative factor pairs.

check.q: Expand $2(a-2)(b-2)$.

steps.title: Pairs
steps.explain: $(1,8)\to(5,12)$; $(2,4)\to(6,8)$. Negative pairs give a side $\le0$. So $2$ pairs.

check.q: Why does $(a-4,b-4)=(-2,-4)$ fail?

2008B23.bridge: Factor with Simon's trick and list factor pairs.
2008B23.recognize: Equations like $xy+px+qy=r$: Simon's favourite factoring trick.

2008B24.goal: $AB=BC=CD$, $\angle ABC=70^\circ$, $\angle BCD=170^\circ$; we want $\angle BAD$. Complete $BCD$ to a rhombus and spot an equilateral triangle.

tools.name: Rhombus
tools.why: $BC=CD$, so the parallelogram has equal sides.

tools.name: Isosceles triangle
tools.why: Both equal the common side length.

2008B24.approach: Build rhombus $BCDE$. Then $\angle CBE=10^\circ$, so $\angle ABE=60^\circ$ and $ABE$ is equilateral. Triangle $AED$ has $EA=ED$ and $\angle AED=360^\circ-60^\circ-170^\circ=130^\circ$, so $\angle EAD=25^\circ$.

steps.title: Equilateral triangle
steps.explain: In rhombus $BCDE$, $\angle CBE=180^\circ-\angle BCD=10^\circ$. So $\angle ABE=60^\circ$ with $AB=BE$: equilateral.

check.q: In a rhombus with one angle $170^\circ$, what is the adjacent angle?

steps.title: Isosceles triangle $AED$
steps.explain: Around $E$: $\angle AEB=60^\circ$, $\angle BED=170^\circ$, so $\angle AED=130^\circ$. Base angles $25^\circ$. $\angle BAD=60^\circ+25^\circ=85^\circ$.

check.q: An isosceles triangle with apex $130^\circ$ has base angles of?

2008B24.bridge: Complete to a rhombus, find the equilateral triangle, then the isosceles one.
2008B24.recognize: Several equal sides with awkward angles: add a point to make a rhombus or equilateral triangle.

2008B25.goal: Michael walks at $5$ ft/s; a truck drives at $10$ ft/s and stops $30$ s at each pail ($200$ ft apart). At $t=0$ Michael is at a pail and the truck is leaving the next one. We count meetings by tracking the gap.

tools.name: Gap per phase
tools.why: Relative speed $+5$ while driving, $-5$ while stopped.

tools.name: Sign changes
tools.why: They meet whenever the gap hits zero.

2008B25.approach: Start gap $200$. Each $50$-s cycle: $+100$ then $-150$. Track the gap at the end of each phase until it stays negative.

steps.title: Approach
steps.explain: Gaps: $200\to300\to150\to250\to100\to200\to50\to150\to0$. First meeting at the end of the 4th stop.

check.q: After each full cycle, how much does the gap shrink?
From gap $-150$, can a $+100$ drive phase bring the gap to $0$?

2008B25.bridge: Record the gap after every phase and count zeros.
2008B25.shortcut: Once the gap is below $-100$ after a stop, a drive phase can't catch up again.
traps: Counting the touch at $0$ followed by moving apart twice.
Ignoring meetings while the truck drives.
2008B25.recognize: Stop-and-go chases: track the gap phase by phase.
